mainTopic: When an אומן or אריס gains a חזקה, and when someone with a stake in land may testify
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of a craftsman (אומן) holding a garment. The word 'ראה' (he saw) in the ברייתא supports the craftsmen of פומבדיתא. רב אשי shows how a clever owner can turn his case into a 'saw' case. רב אחא בריה דרב אויא shows how the craftsman can block that trick. Next the גמרא asks why an אריס (sharecropper) cannot gain a חזקה, and רבי יוחנן answers that the rule is about family sharecroppers. רב נחמן rules that an אריס who installs other sharecroppers in his place does gain a חזקה. רבי יוחנן rules that one who divides the field among sharecroppers does not, since he may just be a manager. The גמרא then asks whether an אריס may testify, and it settles that this depends on whether there is produce in the field. Finally, a ברייתא marked by the memory word עמלק lists people who may testify about land only when the person they help has other land: a guarantor, a lender, and a first buyer. The list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא says 'he saw'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the word 'ראה' in the ברייתא to support the craftsmen of פומבדיתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the earlier position by pointing to one word in a ברייתא: 'ראה,' meaning 'he saw.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the owner a valid claim only when he and witnesses actually saw his garment with the craftsman. If he never saw it, he cannot claim it just because it might be his. This supports the craftsmen of פומבדיתא.

keyTerms.meaning: He saw. Here it means the owner actually saw his garment in the craftsman's hands.
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה.

phrases.english: 'He saw' is what was taught.
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא quoted earlier on the daf, about seeing your garment at the launderer's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion (from before this section) about the craftsmen of פומבדיתא.
steps.raayaObject: The position of the craftsmen of פומבדיתא, that the owner has a claim only when the item was seen in the craftsman's possession.

steps.title: רב אשי: a clever owner can turn it into a 'saw' case
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says a smart owner can get the craftsman to bring out the garment, so that the owner now 'sees' it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: If the owner is clever, he can make it a case of 'he saw.' He says to the craftsman: 'Why are you holding it? Isn't it because I owe you money? Now bring it out and let it be appraised. You take what is yours, and I'll take what is mine.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the owner a trick. He asks the craftsman to bring the garment out for appraisal, so now the owner has seen it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner does not deny the debt. He only asks to settle it fairly by appraisal. Once the craftsman takes out the garment, the case becomes a 'ראה' case, and the ruling changes in the owner's favor.

keyTerms.meaning: Clever, smart.
He makes it into, he turns it into.
You are holding, you have grabbed.
With me (money of yours that I owe).
Appraise them, set a value.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: And if he is clever,
he can make it a case of 'he saw,'
by saying to him: Why are you holding it?
Is it not because you have money with me?
phrases.notes: He means: you're keeping my garment as security for the money I owe you.

phrases.english: Now bring them out and have them appraised,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁקוֹל אַתְּ דִּידָך,ְ וְאֶשְׁקוֹל אֲנָא דִּידִי.
phrases.english: you take yours, and I will take mine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וְאִי חַכִּים, מְשַׁוֵּי לֵיהּ ״רָאָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the 'ראה' rule and shows how an owner can bring himself into it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A clever owner can ask for the garment to be brought out and appraised, which turns his case into a 'he saw' case.

steps.title: The craftsman can refuse: it was already appraised
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא says the craftsman can block רב אשי's trick by saying the garment was already appraised.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, the son of רב אויא, said to רב אשי: The craftsman can answer him: 'I don't need your appraisal. People before you already appraised it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא pushes back on רב אשי. He shows that a clever craftsman can refuse to bring the garment out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's trick works only if the craftsman agrees to bring the garment out. The craftsman can say it was already appraised and found to be worth no more than the debt. Then he never has to show it, and the owner never 'sees' it.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to him.
Appraisal, valuation.
The earlier ones, the ones before.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Avya, said to Rav Ashi:
He can say to him:
I don't need your appraisal,
those who came before you already appraised it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי, מָצֵי אָמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the usefulness of רב אשי's strategy.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Shows that רב אשי's trick does not have to work.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The trick depends on the craftsman agreeing to bring the garment out, and he can refuse by saying it was already appraised.
steps.whatToRemember: The owner can try to force a 'ראה' case by asking for an appraisal, but the craftsman can refuse by saying it was already appraised.

steps.title: Why can't an אריס gain a חזקה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that an אריס has no חזקה and asks why, since he now eats all the produce instead of half.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sharecropper has no חזקה. Why not? Until now he took half, and now he takes all of it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic from the משנה, the sharecropper. It challenges the rule that he cannot gain a חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal אריס eats only half the produce. If for three years he ate all of it, that is not normal sharecropper behavior, so it should show he owns the field. The question is why that does not count as a חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: A sharecropper who works someone's field for a share of the produce.
A presumption of ownership from using the land (usually three years).
Why?
Half.

phrases.english: A sharecropper has no chazaka.
Why?
Until now he took half,
and now he takes all of it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, moving from craftsmen to sharecroppers.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that an אריס has no חזקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eating all the produce instead of half goes beyond what a sharecropper does, so it should prove ownership.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: family sharecroppers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the משנה is talking about family sharecroppers, who normally take in all the produce anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The rule is about family sharecroppers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question by narrowing the case. The משנה means a special kind of sharecropper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A family sharecropper works for one family for many years. He brings all the produce into his own place and then hands over the owner's share. So taking in all the produce is normal for him and proves nothing about ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: Family sharecroppers, who work a family's land over generations.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בַּאֲרִיסֵי בָּתֵּי אָבוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: It is about family sharecroppers.
phrases.notes: Literally 'sharecroppers of fathers' houses,' meaning ones who have worked for the same family for a long time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בַּאֲרִיסֵי בָּתֵּי אָבוֹת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a specific type of sharecropper.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every sharecropper who ate all the produce for three years should gain a חזקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of family sharecroppers, for whom collecting all the produce is normal, so it proves nothing.
steps.whatToRemember: A family sharecropper cannot gain a חזקה, because taking in all the produce is his normal routine.

steps.title: רב נחמן: a sharecropper who brings in other sharecroppers
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that a sharecropper who puts other sharecroppers in his place does gain a חזקה, because an owner would not stay silent about that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: A sharecropper who brought in other sharecroppers in his place has a חזקה. What is the reason? A person does not let sharecroppers be brought onto his land and stay silent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a new ruling: in this case, a sharecropper can gain a חזקה. Then the גמרא explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An owner might ignore his own sharecropper's habits. But strangers being brought in to work his land is something he would protest. If he stayed silent, that shows the first sharecropper really owns the land.

keyTerms.meaning: Brought down, installed (put others to work the land).
What is the reason?
Stays silent (does not protest).

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
A sharecropper who brought in sharecroppers in his place
has a chazaka.
What is the reason?
Because a person does not act this way:
that sharecroppers come down onto his land and he stays silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אָרִיס שֶׁהוֹרִיד אֲרִיסִין תַּחְתָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining when an אריס has no חזקה, gives a case where he does.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sharecropper who installs other sharecroppers in his place gains a חזקה, since an owner would protest strangers on his land.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a חזקה depends on whether the owner's silence makes sense. When a normal owner would protest, his silence becomes evidence.
steps.whatToRemember: An אריס usually has no חזקה, but if he brought in other sharecroppers and the owner said nothing, he does.

steps.title: A sharecropper who divides the field among other sharecroppers gains no חזקה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that an אריס who hands the field out to other sharecroppers does not gain a חזקה, since the owner may have made him a manager.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: A sharecropper who divided the field among other sharecroppers does not get a חזקה. Why? We can say the owner simply made him a manager.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a ruling about an אריס who divided the field among other sharecroppers. Then the גמרא explains his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רב נחמן gave a חזקה to an אריס who put other sharecroppers in his place. Here the אריס divided the field among sharecroppers. רבי יוחנן says that proves nothing, because the owner might simply have made him a manager, and a manager also hands out the work.

keyTerms.meaning: A sharecropper who works someone else's field for a share of the produce
A legal presumption of ownership based on using the land
A manager or administrator put in charge of the property
What is the reason?
Merely, simply

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with רב נחמן in step 6. There the אריס put others in his place and gained a חזקה. Here he divided the field among sharecroppers, which a manager would also do, so he gains no חזקה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
A sharecropper who divided the field among sharecroppers
does not have a presumption of ownership.
What is the reason?
Say that they merely appointed him as a manager.
phrases.notes: "They" means the owner. A manager is allowed to hand out the work, so doing it doesn't make him look like the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אָרִיס שֶׁחִלֵּק לַאֲרִיסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with רב נחמן's ruling in step 6. Dividing the field among sharecroppers, unlike installing them in his place, gives no חזקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אריס who divides the field among other sharecroppers gains no חזקה, because he may simply be a manager.

steps.title: Can a sharecropper testify about the field's ownership?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא sends a question to רב נחמן בר יעקב: is an אריס allowed to testify?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא sent a message to רב נחמן בר יעקב: Let our teacher teach us. Can a sharecropper testify, or can he not testify?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a question someone sent. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the אריס has a personal stake in the field. If the owner he works for loses the land, he may lose his job and his share. So the question is whether that interest makes his testimony unreliable.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent to him (a written question)
Let our teacher instruct us
Testifies, is allowed to be a witness

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda sent
to Rav Nachman bar Yaakov:
Let our teacher instruct us:
Does a sharecropper testify, or does he not testify?
phrases.notes: He means testifying about who owns the field this sharecropper is working.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the אריס as a witness instead of as someone claiming a חזקה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an אריס is a valid witness about the ownership of the field he works.

steps.title: רב יוסף quotes שמואל: a sharecropper may testify
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף, who was sitting there, answers in the name of שמואל that an אריס may testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף was sitting before him and said: This is what שמואל said: A sharecropper can testify.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question by quoting a ruling of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, the אריס's connection to the field does not disqualify him. This answer will be challenged right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him, in his presence
This is what he said

phrases.english: Rav Yosef was sitting before him;
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב נחמן בר יעקב, the one who received the question.

phrases.english: he said to him:
This is what Shmuel said:
A sharecropper can testify.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל ruled that an אריס can testify.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a sharecropper cannot testify
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted that says the opposite of שמואל: an אריס cannot testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: He cannot testify!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges שמואל's ruling with a ברייתא that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא carries great weight. So if it clearly says an אריס cannot testify, שמואל's ruling seems to go against it.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: He cannot testify!

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that an אריס can testify
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא directly states that an אריס cannot testify, which contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: It depends on whether there is produce in the field
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction is resolved. The ברייתא speaks of a time when produce is in the field, and שמואל speaks of a time when there is none.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ruling is where there is produce on the land, and that ruling is where there is no produce on the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that שמואל and the ברייתא are talking about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When crops are standing in the field, the אריס would lose his share if the owner lost the land. That personal gain makes him unfit to testify, which is the ברייתא's case. When there is no produce, he has nothing to gain right now, so he may testify, which is שמואל's case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources speak about different cases
Produce, crops
Land, the field

steps.whatToRemember: An אריס may testify about the field's ownership only when there is no produce in it. When there are crops he stands to gain from, he cannot testify.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is where there is produce on the land,
phrases.notes: "This" is the ברייתא that says he cannot testify. With crops in the field, he has something to gain.

phrases.english: and that is where there is no produce on the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא – הָא דְּאִיכָּא פֵּירָא בְּאַרְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source applies to a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל and the ברייתא seemed to disagree about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא disqualifies the אריס when there is produce in the field; שמואל allows him when there is none.

steps.title: A memory sign for the cases coming next
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the word עמלק as a memory aid for the list of cases it is about to discuss.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא gives a memory sign to help us remember the order of the next cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter of עמלק hints at one case in the coming teaching: ערב (guarantor), מלוה (lender), לוקח (buyer), and קבלן (a guarantor who can be asked to pay directly). Nothing is ruled here yet.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign, a word that helps you remember a list
The word used as the sign; its letters stand for the coming cases

phrases.english: (Amalek is a mnemonic)
phrases.notes: The letters ע, מ, ל, ק hint at the coming cases: ערב, מלוה, לוקח, קבלן. Some versions leave out this line in round brackets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the sharecropper discussion and prepares the next section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. It is a memory sign for the cases about to be discussed.

steps.title: A guarantor may testify for the borrower if the borrower has other land
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a ערב may testify that a field belongs to the לוה. This only works if the לוה owns other land.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A guarantor may testify for the borrower, but only when the borrower has other land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through the list it just marked with the memory word עמלק. The first case is the ערב, the guarantor of a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the לוה loses his land, the lender could come and collect from the ערב, so the ערב seems to gain from his own testimony. But if the לוה has other land, the lender can collect from that instead. Then the ערב gains nothing either way and may testify.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantor, who promises to pay the loan if the borrower doesn't
The borrower
Other land

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A guarantor may testify for the borrower,
phrases.notes: He is testifying that a certain field belongs to the borrower.

phrases.english: but only when he has other land.
phrases.notes: "He" is the borrower. The lender can collect from that other land, so the guarantor is safe either way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins listing the cases that the memory word עמלק pointed to. ע stands for ערב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ערב may testify that land belongs to the לוה, as long as the לוה has other land the lender can collect from.

steps.title: A lender may testify for the borrower if the borrower has other land
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא rules that a מלוה may testify that a field belongs to the לוה, again only if the לוה owns other land.
steps.simpleTranslation: A lender may testify for the borrower, but only when the borrower has other land.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the second case on the list, the lender himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender wants the borrower to keep land so he has something to collect his loan from. If this field is the borrower's only land, the lender is biased. If the borrower has other land, the lender's loan is covered anyway, so his testimony is trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: The lender
Testifies

phrases.english: A lender may testify for the borrower,
but only when he has other land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second case of the same ברייתא. מ in עמלק stands for מלוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מלוה may testify that land belongs to the לוה, as long as the לוה has other land to collect from.

steps.title: The first buyer may testify for the second buyer if the second buyer has other land
steps.stepSummary: Two people bought land from the same seller. The ברייתא rules that the לוקח ראשון may testify for the לוקח שני, but only if the second buyer has other land from that seller.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first buyer may testify for the second buyer, but only when the second buyer has other land.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the third case on the list, two buyers who bought from the same seller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seller owes money, his creditor collects first from the land sold last, which is the second buyer's land. If the second buyer loses this field, the creditor would come after the first buyer's field instead, so the first buyer is biased. If the second buyer has other land from the seller, the creditor can collect from that, and the first buyer may testify.

keyTerms.meaning: The first buyer
The second buyer, who bought later from the same seller

steps.whatToRemember: The three cases so far follow one rule. A person connected to the land may testify, as long as the person he helps has other land. Then the witness has nothing to gain or lose. The ברייתא's list (the ק of עמלק, קבלן) continues on the next amud.
steps.confusionAlert: The two buyers are not buying the same field. Each bought a different field from the same seller, and the question is which field the seller's creditor will take.

phrases.english: The first buyer may testify for the second buyer,
phrases.notes: Both bought fields from the same seller, and someone is now claiming the second buyer's field.

phrases.english: but only when he has other land.
phrases.notes: The second buyer has another field bought from that seller, so the creditor can take that one instead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third case of the same ברייתא. ל in עמלק stands for לוקח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לוקח ראשון may testify for a לוקח שני, as long as the second buyer has other land from the seller that the seller's creditor can collect from.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the basic rule of a biased witness. What matters is whether the witness actually gains or loses from the outcome, not just whether he is connected to the case.
